properties.name: reflow2-mcp --remote: an agent's stdio session works a design on a remote reflow2 server, over HTTPS, carrying a key it never sees
properties.rationale:
Anthony, 2026-09-26: "hold flo2 and reflow2 until the local client is built. Walk me through that step by step", then "Yes, go with (a)" — HTTPS inside reflow2's own client, only in remote mode, trusting the OS certificate store.

FOUND BY RUNNING THE WHOLE CHAIN, NOT BY READING IT: the first end-to-end run broke on the first reply. flo2's gateway pretty-prints its JSON (legal over HTTP), and a multi-line reply split into broken lines on the agent's one-message-per-line stdio channel.

FOUND BY READING THE DESIGN BEFORE SHIPPING: the first draft re-joined and RE-SENT after any failure once a session existed — the shape of fact:root-cause-an-idle-session-expires-and-the-proxy-silently-takes-a-new-seat-so-live-claims-read-gone, and worse here, because re-sending a change after a timeout can apply it twice. It now re-joins only on the 404 the MCP spec defines as "this session is gone". The shared-mode proxy still retries after any failure (with a daemon restart); unchanged, and not in this change.
properties.summary:
`--remote <url>` with `--api-key-env VAR` or `--api-key-file PATH` (cap:a-local-client-reaches-a-remote-server), step 1 of req:a-local-client-works-against-a-remote-reflow2-server-by-url. mcp_http.rs gains https:// endpoints (rustls 0.23 with ring, tokio-rustls 0.26, rustls-native-certs 0.8 — three new dependencies, used only in remote mode), a bearer header, readable 401/403/404 errors, one-line re-serialization of any plain-JSON reply, and a typed SessionGone error for the transport's forgotten-session 404. proxy.rs gains the remote forwarding loop, which re-joins only on SessionGone.

TESTED: tests/a_local_client_works_against_a_remote_server.rs, 9 tests against a stand-in server that records what it is sent, plus unit tests. Driven end to end on this machine (client → flo2's gateway from main in dev mode → a real 0.71.0 reflow2): initialize, tools/list (176 tools through the engine door), add_requirement credited AUTHORED_BY to the token's own contributor, import_graph refused at the door, the write log holding add_contributor and add_requirement, the key absent from the client's stderr. Live against https://api.flo2.io/mcp: TLS verified through the OS store, and an unauthenticated call came back as a readable 401 error.
